expectations.text: Identifies this as a potential 'severe incident' under Art. 14(5): impact on the product's ability to protect availability/authenticity/integrity/confidentiality of sensitive data or functions, or introduction/execution of malicious code — update infrastructure compromise plainly qualifies
expectations.evidence: 'Article 14(5) defines a severe incident... impact on the ability to protect sensitive data or functions, or the introduction/execution of malicious code. A ransomware compromise of your update-distribution infrastructure fits this squarely'

expectations.text: Gives the severe-incident clock: 24-hour early warning, 72-hour notification, and final report within ONE MONTH after the 72-hour notification (distinct from the 14-day post-fix rule for exploited vulnerabilities)
expectations.evidence: 'T+24 hours... Early warning'; 'T+72 hours... Full incident notification'; 'T+1 month after the 72-hour notification — Post-incident report... different from the exploited-vulnerability track, where the final report is tied to when a corrective measure becomes available'

expectations.text: States reporting goes through the ENISA Single Reporting Platform to the main-establishment CSIRT and ENISA, in force since September 11, 2026
expectations.evidence: 'Through the ENISA SRP... live since 11 September 2026'; 'selects the CSIRT Designated as Coordinator for your Member State of main establishment'; 'Notifications go simultaneously to your CSIRT coordinator and ENISA'

expectations.text: Distinguishes CRA reporting from other regimes where relevant (e.g., GDPR breach notification or NIS2 may apply in parallel to different actors/facts)
expectations.evidence: No mention of GDPR, NIS2, or any parallel reporting regime anywhere in the response

expectations.text: Notes awareness-based timing and advises documenting the awareness moment and assessment
expectations.evidence: States 'clock starts at awareness, not at compromise' but never advises documenting the awareness moment/assessment (no 'document'/'timestamp' advice; the only documentation reference is Annex I technical documentation for update integrity)
